mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: Establish who seems in control, then let their own choice reverse it
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: An unexplained stronger character solves everything

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: Show the audience a clue the character misses; let behavior build the gap
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: Concealing the only useful clue until the last frame

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: Each unnecessary improvement creates a new cost with visual consequences
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: Three versions of the same failed push

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: Define an instruction clearly, then exploit a coherent second meaning
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: Wordplay that the image cannot support

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: Two characters pursue understandable incompatible goals in one space
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: One character exists only to be arbitrarily foolish

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: A local fix spreads into a larger problem
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: Random chaos without object or causal continuity

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: A resourceful solution works, but changes the original objective
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: Failure after failure with no learning or agency

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: A seemingly minor early action returns at the worst possible moment
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: A new hazard appears with no plant

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: Ordinary objects become meaningful obstacles at a miniature scale
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: Size changes between shots to force a gag

mechanisms.how_to_make_it_playable: After a decisive climax, a short secondary beat reframes the result
mechanisms.failure_to_reject: A long explanation after the joke already landed
